R221.note: ExecuteSqlInterpolatedAsync correctly parameterizes AccountId/Status/BeforeUtc via FormattableString, matching the stated contract with no other behavior change.

R222.note: scanf("%15s",...) bounds the write and prevents the overflow, but for a token longer than 15 chars it silently truncates and returns success (leaving the remainder unread in stdin) instead of rejecting with -1 as the contract requires; not disclosed.

R223.note: res.sendFile(requestedFile, {root: reportsDir}) is Express's documented containment mechanism; removal of the now-dead path.join line is stated and harmless.

R224.note: Standard HTML-entity escaping applied only to the untrusted closingNote before interpolation; correct sink, no other observable change.

R225.note: ValidAlgorithms pinned to RS256 is the correct, real TokenValidationParameters property for closing alg-confusion; legitimate RS256 tokens still validate and failures still throw, matching the contract.

R226.note: offset + length > capacity is the right shape for the stated combination check, but offset and length are both size_t and the addition can wrap around on an extreme attacker-supplied offset, bypassing the check (should also test offset > capacity or length > capacity - offset); no other behavior change for the normal-range case.

R227.note: Fixed code calls tree.GetCompilationUnitSyntax(), which does not exist on SyntaxTree (verified by building against Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp 5.9.0: CS1061, real API is GetCompilationUnitRoot()), so the fix does not compile; separately, the syntax denylist is trivially bypassed by assigning a blocked method to a delegate/variable and invoking through that identifier instead.

R228.note: Verified with real GNU tar: 'tar czf out.tar -- -czf' archives a file literally named '-czf' rather than treating it as options; -- placed before filenames.extend is the correct, minimal fix.

R229.note: crypto/rand.Read correctly closes the weak-PRNG issue, but the contract requires a 32-character key drawn from the original alphabet and the fix instead emits a 64-character hex string - a disclosed but contract-breaking format/length change.

R230.note: is_relative_to(BASE_DIR) after resolve(strict=True) correctly blocks absolute-path and traversal escapes, but resolve(strict=True) doesn't check the target is a regular file (unlike the original os.path.isfile), so requesting an existing directory now raises an uncaught IsADirectoryError (500) instead of the original clean 404 - not mentioned.

R231.note: unique_ptr->shared_ptr with capture-by-value is the canonical fix and exactly the ownership-sharing option the contract allows; single enqueue preserved, signature change is the disclosed and necessary consequence of that approach.

R232.note: Drops the shell entirely and passes convert's arguments as a plain exec.Command array; closes the reported shell-injection sink with no other observable change.

R233.note: Extension now derived solely from the server-validated detectedType map rather than the client filename, closing the dangerous-extension vector; behavior for legitimate uploads is unchanged or corrected, not broken.

R234.note: Removing mark_safe() blocks the injected script (wrong shape though: escaping should target announcement_text, not the whole markup), but Django's autoescaping then escapes the intentional wrapper markup too, so every legitimate banner now renders as literal escaped text (e.g. '<div...') instead of a styled div - a silent regression to normal use, not mentioned.

R235.note: resolve_entities=False (plus load_dtd=False, no_network=True) is lxml's standard XXE mitigation and fully closes the sink without changing parsing of well-formed XML that doesn't rely on external entities.

R236.note: Textbook PreparedStatement parameterization; return value and no-result branch unchanged.

R237.note: SHA256 hash allowlist before Assembly.Load is an appropriate mitigation given no sandboxing is available on net8.0, but it repurposes the endpoint - stated purpose was letting an admin upload and run a newly compiled plugin, and now only pre-approved (already-hashed) binaries can load, so uploading any new plugin fails; disclosed as the intended mechanism but not flagged as a functional change to the endpoint's stated purpose.

R238.note: Key($publicKey,'RS256') pins the algorithm, closing the confusion; the RS256 path is unchanged, and the only algorithm actually dropped (HS256 verified against the wrong key, rsaPublicKey) was already non-functional for legitimate use in the original code, so no working path regresses.
